Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, as well as the source location. The measurement has a higher latitude than the source likely due to deflection and that a higher latitude was necessary to include the entire width of the event.
Approximate parameters as source has not been found and the CME front is very faint in most timestamps.

Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, and loosely based on a possible source location near S28W05. This measurement is uncertain due to the unclear source location. It is also possible this event is far-sided but the best fit was found using an Earth-facing longitude.
Measurement based on the source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. SOHO LASCO C3 was not usable in this measurement as the CME was obscured by the pylon.

Shock front measurement, which presents as a faint halo out in front of the bulk, wrapping all the way around to the westward portion of the coronagraph imagery. Longitude was increased from -70 degrees westward until the westward-most portion of the shock fit in SWPC_Cat.
Two-spacecraft leading measurement which considers that the eruption is on the far-side.

The leading edge of this CME is only visible for a few frames in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 due to its speed. SOHO LASCO C3 was experiencing a reduced cadence of one frame per three hours. Unable to obtain reliable measurement from limited C3 difference imagery, so best fit was made using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 only.

Measurement made using best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. Difficult to get a good measurement for this CME due to the changing shape of the bulk and limited imagery from the coronagraphs (CME moves quickly thru C2, not visible to measure in C3 difference imagery, data gap in COR2A limits measurement to three frames where CME is in the FOV).
Measurement of the bulk/core of the CME ignoring the wider and fainter shock using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2; inclusion of the wider shock provided a much larger positive longitude.

Leading edge measurement encompassing bulk to the southwest as well as faint shock front due south and southeast using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. Due to nature of this measurement with bulk to southwest and fainter shock portion to south, expected impacts at Earth may be overestimated by simulation.

Measurement made attempting best fit between coronagraphs. Reduced cadence in SOHO LASCO C3 results in low resolution difference imagery. The few frames that the leading edge of the CME is in C2's FOV are corrupt, rendering C2 difference imagery unusable for reliable measuring.

Leading edge measurement encompassing the entire width of the CME using late frames of SOHO C2, C3 and STEREO A COR2 up to about 01:30Z. The CME moves so quickly it is not measurable in SOHO C2 in many frames.
This event is partially obscured by CME: 2023-07-18T20:36Z so it is possible the half-width is slightly larger than what was visible in coronagraph imagery and measured.
Best fit of the shock separating out from the bulk given only SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery, no frames of the shock were available in STEREO COR2A.
Best fit of the shock separating out from the bulk given only SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery, no frames of the shock were available in STEREO COR2A.
Preliminary measurement of the CME shock based on the assumption that this is a front-sided CME and on the fit in swpc_cat

Analysis of the brighter second front of this CME which is likely its bulk. Analysis is based on the location of the eruption near AR 3376 (NW) but is adjusted to make a fit in swpc_cat in coronagraphs.
A very uncertain analysis since the source (filament eruption) is seen either on or behind the limb in EUVIA 195 and the longitude can vary by 10-20 degrees (on/behind the limb).
Analysis of the brighter SW feature that is likely the bulk of the CME taking into account the location of the former AR 3363 (155-160 deg), per GONG farside imagery/analysis.
Analysis of the bulk/leading edge of the CME.

A very uncertain analysis assuming the source is the relatively minor eruption NW of Active Region 13386 marked by high rising post-eruptive arcades and dimming. This source is not certain since it is relatively minor, however no alternative source has been found.
Measurement of the brightest feature/bulk of the CME using two spacecraft.

Measurement based on source location of flare and eruption, around longitude W75, due to lack of stereoscopic analysis capability. The shock and leading edge of this CME appear to be indistinguishable, and so they were measured together. This CME was not measured in STEREO A due to a data gap, as the leading edge of the CME had left the field of view after the gap.
Measurement with longitude based off on source location, AR 3386, currently around W90.
Very preliminary measurement of the bulk. This CME is measured with an approximated longitude due to a lack of stereoscopic viewpoints.
Very preliminary measurement of the bulk. This CME is measured with an approximated longitude due to a lack of stereoscopic viewpoints.

The longitude for this measurement is approximate, as the source location was estimated based on the location of Active Region 13386 which rotated off the Earth-facing disk on 2023-08-07. The longitude may vary +/-10 degrees as a result.
Measurement of what is likely the shock of this CME, which appears to be traveling slightly more northward than the brighter, slower bulk of the CME in the field of view of the coronagraphs.

Updated parameters with additional imagery. Longitudes range between 35-55 degrees depending on feature tracked. The shock feature is likely closer to the 35 degree longitudes. Front becomes diffuse in much later frames in SOHO LASCO C3.

Updated parameters with additional imagery. Longitudes range between 35-55 degrees depending on feature tracked. The shock feature is likely closer to the 35 degree longitudes. Front becomes diffuse in much later frames in SOHO LASCO C3.
Bulk measurement of CME. Longitude may vary due to limited stereoscopic viewpoints of CME and source.
Bulk measurement of CME. Longitude may vary due to limited stereoscopic viewpoints of CME and source.
Measurement of the leading edge using a potential source location of old AR 3413, potentially currently around longitude 120-125.

One spacecraft measurement assuming the source is associated with old AR 3413, potentially around longitude 125-130. A high half-width was required to achieve the shape of the leading edge and to obtain a similar longitude as was obtained for the CME: 2023-09-05T14:00Z event, though a far-sided longitude closer to 160 but a less excessive half-width is also a possible source. The lower longitude also fits observations better as we seen the front off the western limb.

SWPC_CAT measurement using SOHO LASCO C3 imagery only. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available for this measurement. The longitude is approximate and chosen based on NSO GONG data indicating possible far-sided activity, lack of visible source eruption on the Earth-facing disk, and best fit in SWPC_CAT.
Measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Longitude is based on source location,
Measurement using only 3 frames each of SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 due to the faintness of the CME.
Measurement based on a possible far-sided source location, focusing on the bulk portion of this event. The measured longitude was estimated based on GONG far-sided imagery and is therefore uncertain.

The longitude was estimated based on the best fit in coronagraph imagery. The source is visible beyond the E/NE limb, but a precise source location is unknown since this event is far-sided. The measured longitude may therefore vary by +/-10 degrees.
This measurement focuses on the bulk portion of this event. As the source eruption occurs near the limb and extends over a large area, the measured longitude may vary by +/-10 degrees.
Measurement using best fit between coronagraphs and estimate of source from EUV imagery. Shock and bulk are a bit irregular but appear to be moving close together.

Measurement of what is likely the shock of this CME. Longitude approximated by best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT. NSO GONG data also shows a region of interest on the far side that may be a candidate for this eruption.

Updated measurement with the full SOHO LASCO C2/C3 downlink now available, which allowed for some better triangulation using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A imagery far into the FOV. The measured longitude was found to be deflected slightly eastward from the eruption site, and particularly wide. In this later analysis we found it difficult to differentiate between the shock front and leading edge in available real-time imagery.

Bulk measurement made using source location and best fit between coronagraphs. Southern deflection from source location is likely associated with the southern direction of EUV wave propagation as seen in UV imagery.
This analysis is very uncertain since the absence of STEREO data, CME complex shape seemingly not corresponding to the available coronal signatures make it hard to interpret it with certainty.

Shock measurement using source location seen in UV imagery and best fit between coronagraphs. This shock front has a slightly asymmetrical shape. There is inherent uncertainty in this measurement due to the head-on directionality of the CME (i.e. being a partial halo).
These parameters are based off of the best fit of the faint SHOCK feature seen in SOHO and STEREO A coronagraph difference imagery.
These parameters are based off of the best fit of the BULK seen in SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2 coronagraph difference imagery.

These parameters are based off of the best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. However, the feature deflects NE as it progresses out in the field of view, making these parameters very uncertain. The feature appears to have a half-width less than 10 degrees at the start, but fills the 10 degree half-width lasso in SWPC_CAT in later frames.

Measurement of the SHOCK using best fit in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery and source location. This CME is not captured by STEREO A COR2 imagery due to a data gap lasting from 2024-01-23T03:53Z to 2024-01-23T12:23Z.

Measurement based on the source location. Only a few frames were available for this measurement in SOHO LASCO C2 as the CME is obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3. Additionally, there is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The measured longitude may vary by +/-10 degrees as a result.
Updated measurement of the bulk portion using a longitude closer to the source location.

Updated measurement of the shock front using a longitude closer to the source location. Multiple measurements of the shock portion range in longitude from 25 to 50 degrees with speeds ranging from 1454 km/s to 1888 km/s.

Analysis of the more eastern, brighter portion of this CME, based on the likely backsided source location indicated by geoseismology data - a large active region seen for days in GONG farside imagery and at longitude ~-150 deg on 01-30. With the coronal signatures indicating a backsided region in the SW, we based our swpc_cat analysis with one coronagraph (SOHO LASCO) on the longitude of this likely active region and on the assumption that the half width of the CME is 45 degrees. This analysis is of course uncertain.

Analysis of a wider, fainter shock front of this CME that forms a full halo in SOHO LASCO. Analysis is based on a good fit in swpc_cat in one coronagraph and the resulting longitude is more backsided than the assumed source location derived from GONG farside helioseismology imagery.

Measurement of the BULK based on source location in UV imagery and best fit between coronagraphs, especially using later frames of SOHO LASCO C3 difference imagery (see clear loop in C3 difference frame: 2024-02-02T14:42Z). Temporary broadening of cadence in STEREO A COR2 imagery caused leading edge to be very faint in running difference imagery.

Measured using the source of AR 3575 at the time of eruption and triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A, noting some eastward deflection that was observed in SDO imagery. Due to the speed and angle towards both coronagraphs, not many frames were able to be used before reaching the 21.5 Rs height.
Measurement using the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Measurement of the bulk of the CME, which was analyzed to be narrower than the fainter shock of the CME.
Measurement of wider, fainter shock.

Uncertain analysis of the faint wispy shock preceding the bulk front. This analysis does not include the wider halo feature associated with this CME that seems to be even more backsided, based on fitting it in swpc_cat.
Analysis with additional coronagraph imagery.
Measurement of leading edge using best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 beyond the east limb.
This is a measurement of the wider, faint shock of the CME.
Preliminary measurement of the SHOCK feature.
Measurement of BULK feature using candidate source location and best fit between coronagraphs.
An uncertain analysis of halo-like fainter shock with one coronagraph in swpc_cat because of data gaps in other coronagraphs and with source being behind the east limb.
Measurement of leading edge using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The bulk of the CME is wider than the shock, which extends to almost a full halo in the coronagraphs.
Measurement of the wider, faster, fainter shock of the CME.
Measurement using best fit between coronagraphs. Tricky fit in STEREO A COR2.

Measurement of the bulk portion based on the approximate location of former Active Region 13575 combined with the best fit in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery. There is no clear, distinguishable shock feature measured for this CME. There is a lack of stereoscopic imagery for this event due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2.

Approximate measurement of wider fainter shock of this CME based on fit in one coronagraph (SOHO LASCO). No STEREO A COR2 imagery is available for this event at the time because of a data gap from 2024-02-17T11:55Z.

Updated analysis of bulk based on later SOHO LASCO C3 imagery, focuses on the likely wider bulk of the CME including previously excluded NE feature of the CME. One coronagraph analysis since no STEREO A coronagraph imagery available because of a large data gap.
Note that the second outflow/front seen in SOHO LASCO C3 around 15:08Z also measured with similar parameters and was not separately added to the database.

Measurement of the leading edge of the bulk of the CME based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 as well as potential source location of old AR 3575, currently around approximately -135 to -130 degrees longitude.
Measurement of the wider, fainter, partial halo shock of the CME, not the bulk.

Measurement of the bulk using estimate of source location with southward deflection as seen in UV imagery and best fit between coronagraphs. Leading edge is only visible for 2 frames in STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery due to a data gap lasting from 2024-02-20T13:53Z to 2024-02-21T03:23Z.
One coronagraph (SOHO LASCO) analysis based on the apparent location of the source just behind the limb.
Very approximate analysis based on fitting of a faint fuzzy shock front with one coronagraph (SOHO) in swpc_cat tool.

Aalysis based on location of possible source east of active region 3603. We only have one coronagraph available since the CME is covered by a data gap in STEREO A. Upon more deliberations, this analysis was deemed too unreliable. The source could be behind the SW limb where there is some faint opening of field lines after 2024-03-10T21:40Z.

Measurement of the SHOCK front portion. Multiple shock measurements resulted in longitudes spanning 98 to 122 degrees with speeds ranging from 1321 km/s to 1201 km/s. The longitude may vary slightly due to possible deflection.

Measurement of BULK feature using best fit in coronagraph imagery with approximate source location of AR 13599 W110 as reference. Only one frame of STEREO A COR2 difference imagery was available for this measurement due to a data gap lasting from 2024-03-15T03:38Z to 2024-03-15T07:23Z.

A very uncertain 3D analysis. It was made with one coronagraph only (SOHO LASCO C3) in swpc_cat tool and based on the assumptions that the source of this CME is the prominence eruption seemingly off/just behind the SW limb, also assuming that the prominence originates in Active Region 3599 (at longitude ~96 at the time). Unfortunately, the CME is fully covered by data gap in STEREO and its front not clearly seen in C2 and we are not able to confirm this analysis.

Approximate measurement which follows the brighter bulk portion of this complex-shape event. Measured parameters are based on the source location and the best fit in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery, however the center of the elongated source eruption is not certain. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery during this event so there was no stereoscopic viewpoint available to confirm the measured parameters. The half width of this CME is also not certain.

Analysis of the second (after the X-class flare) bright front first seen to the north in SOHO LASCO C2 coronagraph, which is likely the bulk of the CME. This analysis is based on the best fit in two coronagraphs. Note that only two timestamps with this front are available from STEREO A COR2 because of a data gap. This bright front is also accompanied by a more diffuse, faint likely shock front further southeast, which is analyzed separately.

Approximate analysis of the fainter, more SW, likely shock front of this CME. Analysis is based on the best fit in two coronagraphs, with two timestamps available in STEREO A COR2. We are using default half width of 45 degrees, adding to the uncertainty of this analysis.

Preliminary measurement based on the approximate longitude of former Active Region 13615. This measurement uses only a few available frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery as there are large data gaps in both coronagraphs preventing much of this event from being observed. The measured parameters may vary as a result.

Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A to determine the far-sided source likely observed as such in SDO imagery. Also determined to be far-sided by knowing the potential location of old, very active AR 3615 due to return to the E limb in a few days. Longitude range very close to E100.

Parameters based on best fit of jet-like feature in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. A faint wider portion is visible in difference imagery, but it is unclear if it is associated with this jet-feature or of it is a separate feature on its own.
Parameters based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A difference imagery.
Parameters based on best fit of leading edge in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 difference imagery.
Approximate measurement based on source location of flare on or just beyond the east limb.
Measurement based on the source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Multiple measurements produced speeds ranging from 1074 to 1098 km/s.

Preliminary SHOCK measurement made using both coronagraphs, with limited imagery due to a current gap between SOHO downlinks due to resume at T17:15Z today and recency of the front emerging in all imagery. Source of S22W11 (the M8.6-Class flare) used as a basis finding a good triangulation between coronagraphs near here.
These parameters are based on the best fit of the BULK of the CME. Measured speeds varied between 1200km/s to 1500km/s.
SHOCK parameters based off of best fit in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Measurement of the SHOCK using the source location seen in UV imagery. Only C3 difference imagery used. No imagery available from STEREO A COR2 due to data gap lasting from 2024-05-08T19:53Z to 2024-05-09T01:53Z.

Measurement of the BULK using the source location seen in UV imagery. Only C3 difference imagery used. No imagery available from STEREO A COR2 due to data gap lasting from 2024-05-08T19:53Z to 2024-05-09T01:53Z.
Analysis of the fainter full halo shock front, made by fitting this front in two coronagraphs.

Bulk measurement based on the brightest, inner feature. Measured parameters based on the source eruption and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. Multiple bulk measurements produced speeds ranging from 1018 to 1133 km/s and longitudes spanning from 31 to 37 degrees.

Measurement of the shock portion which extends towards the south and east compared to the bulk. Measured parameters based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2, which deviates east of the source location.

Updated bulk parameters. The CME bulk appears to have an earlobe shape to it with a smoother loop towards the north and a messy front to the south. It is possible these fronts could be interpreted as two separate CMEs overlapping each other, however they travel together in white-light and difference imagery.

This is a SHOCK measurement based on the best fit of shock features in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. Due to the asymmetric shape of the shock front, this measurement leaves out a little bit of the north/northwestern portion of the shock front.

Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs. There seems to be some northward deflection since although the longitude of the fit corresponds well to the longitude of the Active Region 3664 at the time, the latitude of the fit is more northern than the latitude of the region.
Measurement of the BULK using source location seen in UV imagery, which also indicates some southern deflection, and best stereoscopic fit between coronagraphs.
Measurement of the SHOCK of the CME using best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs.

Analysis based on the fit in two coronagraph and on the longitude of the associated significant flare. We do not see the flare source since it is behind the limb so the exact location of the eruption could be somewhat different from the calculated location of the active region behind the limb.
Analysis based on the fit of the faint front in coronagraph and is tentative.
This analysis is based on the calculated longitude of the Active Region 3664, which has rotated behind the west limb.
Measurement using the source of AR 3682 (N18E72) and finding a great triangulation between SOHO and STEREO coronagraphs almost exactly at this point.
Measurement of the BULK using candidate source location AR 13664 approximated longitude of W105, and best fit between coronagraphs.
Measurement of the BULK using candidate source location AR 13664 approximated longitude of W105 and best fit between coronagraphs, finding a good triangulation deflected to W114.
Measurement using best fit between C3 and STEREO A COR2 frames and inference that the source location is farsided based on UV imagery.
Used approximate location of source signature as seen in UV imagery, used candidate source location AR 13664 approximated longitude of W105, and best fit between coronagraphs.
Measurement of the leading edge using approximate location of AR 3664. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available for this measurement.
Final analysis with two coronagraphs now that SOHO LASCO imagery is available.
Measurement using the X2.9 flare from AR 3685 on or just beyond the SE limb as the source, finding a decent fit between STEREO COR2A and the limited available SOHO LASCO C3 imagery.
Parameters obtained based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT, using potential source location beyond limb. The longitude may vary by approx. +/- 10 degrees.
Parameters based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT, based on possible backside source location.
Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT as well as potential source location.
Analysis of the bulk based on the fit in two coronagraphs and confirmed by the calculated current farsided longitude of the former Active Region 13664.
Analysis of the shock of this CME based on the fit in two coronagraphs and confirmed by the calculated farsided longitude of former Active Region 13664.
Measurement made using location of source as seen in UV imagery (S11E65) and best fit of bulk portion as seen in C2 and C3.
Measurement of what was determined to likely be the SHOCK of this CME using backsided source and the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT.
Measurement of the bulk of this CME using best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

Parameters are based on the best fit of the BULK of the CME. The CME exhibits a dimpled front and continues to expand in width as it progresses out of the field of view. Most of the CME's bulk is captured in this analysis, however portions on the left hand boundary were excluded in later frames due to the expansion of the CME.

Parameters based on the SHOCK of the CME. Due to the irregular shape of the CME and shock, some portions of the shock were excluded to attempt a best fit. Parameters may vary due to limitations with measuring techniques.
Parameters of the SHOCK of the CME based on SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 difference imagery.

Somewhat uncertain analysis of the outer, earlier front of this halo CME (possibly its shock), based on the fit with two coronagraphs. Only one coronagraph frame is available for STEREO A COR2 bc of a data gap, adding to the uncertainty of analysis. These parameters are somewhat confirmed by the location of a large backsided active region in helioseismology imagery from GONG which is likely the former AR 13679 that was at lat/lon -8/-170 at the time of event.

Approximate analysis of the second front of this halo CME (possibly its bulk), based on a fit with two coronagraphs. For STEREO A COR2 imagery only one timestamp is available (bc of a large data gap), adding to the uncertainty of analysis. Analysis is supported by the location of a large backsided active region in helioseismology imagery from GONG - likely the former AR 13679 that was around lat/lon -8/-170 at the time of this event. In addition, STIX instrument on Solar Orbiter detected a significant flare at 2024-06-01T18:45Z.

BULK measurement made with more complete SOHO frames in LASCO C2/C3 following its downlink backfill. Very little has changed between the preliminary analysis, finding a good triangulation between SOHO and STEREO coronagraphs here.

SHOCK measurement made with more complete SOHO frames in LASCO C2/C3 following its downlink backfill. This shock front is dimpled between two apparent fronts, seen in both SOHO and STEREO coronagraphs, which made for some difficulty triangulating the two images. Eventually settled on a triangulation using the top of the halo shock as the shared feature between both, finding a good fit.
Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs and on the location of the associated flare.
Very approximate analysis of the likely more backsided shock based on the best fit with two coronagraphs only.
BULK measurement using only SOHO C3 imagery, due to a STEREO COR2A data gap. Source longitude of AR 3697 (S18W96) used as a basis, finding a northward deflection with a good fit.
SHOCK measurement using only SOHO C3 imagery, due to a STEREO COR2A data gap. Source longitude of AR 3697 (S18W96) used as a basis, ultimately fitting much better around W139.
UPDATED BULK measurement using source location approx. longitude of W112, several frames of C3, and the one frame of STEREO A COR2 that had some indication of the leading edge in the frame.
Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The measured longitude may vary slightly as the precise source location is unknown.
Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The measured longitude may vary as there is no precise source location due to the far-sided source.
Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR 2 imagery. The measured parameters may vary slightly as the source is far-sided and there is no precise source location.
The measured longitude is speculative due to the far-sided and uncertain source location. The measured parameters were based on the best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and may vary.

Measurement made using the source of AR 3711 (S12W76) and triangulation between SOHO and STEREO coronagraphs, finding a great fit near this source. This fit is of the more northern of the two fronts sourced from this same eruption.
Measurement of the fainter shock feature based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
This analysis is based on the fit with two coronagraphs for the wider and slightly fainter more full-halo like shock front (vs the more partial halo bulk to the NW in SOHO).
Analysis based on the best fit of the more NE brighter front of this complex-shaped CME with two coronagraphs.
Approximate analysis of the brighter narrower bulk front of this CME based on the best fit in two coronagraphs, somewhat confirmed by the potential source - a behind the ENE limb filament.
Approximate analysis of the fainter and wider likely shock front of this CME based on the fit in two coronagraphs.

Analysis is based on the best fit with two coronagraphs. The fit points to the active region 3752 (N22E63) as the source of this CME, however all coronal signatures indicate a location close to the limb.
Measurement based on source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Parameters based on the potential SHOCK feature using SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 difference imagery. There is uncertainty with this analysis due to lack of stereoscopic viewpoints.

Measurement of the inner bulk feature based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. As the source is far-sided and a precise source location is unknown, the measured parameters may vary slightly.. Multiple measurements produced speeds ranging from 1277 km/s to 1544 km/s and longitudes spanning 170 to 176 degrees.

Measurement of the possible shock feature based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Multiple shock measurements produced speeds ranging from 1544 km/s to 1691 km/s. It is difficult to obtain a decent fit of the entire shock feature in both SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This measurement therefore focuses on the brighter, northern shock feature without compromising on the fit between coronagraphs.
Parameters based on best fit of the bulk feature seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 difference imagery.
Parameters based on shock feature in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 difference imagery. Longitude may vary by +/- 10 degrees based on analysis.
Measurement of wider, fainter SHOCK feature based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Parameters based on source location and best fit of features in SOHO LASCO C3 difference imagery.
Preliminary measurement of the fainter, faster, wider bulk of this CME. Only SOHO LASCO C2/C3  imagery was available for this measurement due to a data gap, so this measurement is approximate.
Measurement of the narrower, northern portion of this CME, based on source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery, there is no stereoscopic viewpoint available to confirm the measurement. Additionally, the northern portion of this event is partially obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

Measurement of the shock front using SOHO LASCO C3 imagery only. Because there is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 and this CME is partially obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3, the measured parameters may vary slightly.

Measurement of the bulk portion based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs. The measured longitude deflects about 15 degrees from the source location, and multiple measurements produced speeds ranging from 1092 km/s to 1120 km/s.
Measurement of the shock front based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

BULK measurement, triangulated between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO COR2A using the source of the eruption from AR 3768 around S14W88 as the source, finding a good fit slightly deflected eastward. This CME front is a bit lopsided to the northern end, so this fit best tracking the leading edge misses some material on the southern portion of the leading edge.
Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Analysis based on the location of the potential source of the flare and eruption - Active Region 3765 and confirmed by a good fit in two coronagraphs with this longitude. The source is behind the limb, but is seen on disk in EUVI STEREO A.

Best fit measurement of extremely diffuse leading edge. Only two frames of COR2A, two frames of C2, and one frame of C3 were able to be used due to the faintness of the event. However, the best fit parameters match the candidate source location well.
Parameters based on best fit of features in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Updated StereoCAT analysis using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. The shock measurement yielded similar parameters, but a wider half-width.
Parameters based on fit using STEREOCAT of faint features. There is a higher degree of uncertainty with these parameters due to faintness of event and limited available frames.
Approximate analysis based on the best fit in two coronagraphs. Longitudes could range from 135 to 150 degrees.
Measurement of the faster, wider, shock feature of this CME.
Shock measurement using SOHO C2, C3, and STEREO A, focusing on a more skillful fit of the shock in SOHO rather than STEREO A.
Updated bulk measurement with a smaller half-width.
Parameters based on best fit of the BULK of the CME. Data gap in SOHO misses CME front in SOHO LASCO C2 entirely.
Parameters based on best fit of the SHOCK of the CME. Portions of the shock are excluded due to measurement technique restraints.

Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. There is no STEREO A COR2 imagery available for this measurement due to a data gap from 2024-09-11T14:38Z to 2024-09-11T22:23Z.
Updated leading edge measurement of the bulk using only SOHO C3 imagery out to 18:30Z.
Updated SHOCK measurement based on source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 using more available imagery.
Measurement of the bulk of the CME based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 in SWPC_CAT.
Measurement of the wider, fainter, SHOCK of the CME.
Leading edge measurement using SOHO C2, C3 and limited STEREO A COR2 frames, as the spacecraft was in a campaign. There appears to be some westward deflection.
Analysis of the second front of this CME (bulk?) based on the location of the source.

A very approximate analysis of the fainter earlier front of this CME based on the source location. Analysis is especially uncertain because of the faintness of the front in STEREO A coronagraph, the sparseness of the COR2A imagery b/c of the campaign mode.
Measurement of shock front using only SOHO imagery, since the CME is not visible well in STEREO A.

Shock measurement using one spacecraft (SOHO) C2 and C3 images which fits the widest extent of the south and southwestern portions of the CME leading edge as well as a north-northeastern portion that reveals itself in later SOHO frames after 22:30Z which is assumed to be part of the CME shock, though it is disjoint. This measurement is in support of solar energetic particle modeling activities, and as such, is not an approximation of the source location and should not be used for trajectory analysis.

Measured longitude based on the approximate source location. There is uncertainty in this measurement due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery and limited imagery in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The measured parameters may therefore vary slightly.

Two-coronagraph analysis of the complex-shaped (two-lobed) brighter front we consider to be the bulk of this CME. This analysis is based on the location of the X flare as the source, which is confirmed by a good fit with two coronagraphs. This analysis encompasses both the more eastern lobe/front of this CME and the more western lobe, which are best seen in LASCO C2.
SHOCK measurement made using running difference imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

Measurement using approximate longitude of source location observed in UV imagery along with the best fit in available frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. The leading edge of this CME was not captured by COR2A due to a data gap.
Very approximate measurement based on the fit in two coronagraphs and confirmed by the possible location of the source (dimming). Only a few timestamps are available for this front in coronagraphs.
Measurement based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2

Two-coronagraph analysis of the western loop-like front/lobe of the complex halo CME complex. Analysis is based on the source location (approximate center of the erupting filament) and confirmed by a decent fit in two coronagraphs. Encompasses only the western lobe/front of this complex (with the more western lobe deemed to be the X-flare associated separate CME).
Parameters based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery of the bulk of the CME. The fainter potential shock portion to the SW is excluded from this analysis.
Parameters based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Parameters based on best fit of features in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
BULK measurement based on source location and the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.

SHOCK MEASUREMENT triangulated between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO COR2A, following the outermost leading edge of the wider, fainter shock traveling ahead of the bulk. This notably does not capture the entire shock-like feature observed in both SOHO and STEREO coronagraphs in the SWPC_CAT measurement tool. This fit follows the leading edge of the shock best, cutting short from the widest portions of the partial halo.

Measurement of the bulk portion based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This event is wide and difficult to fit between coronagraphs, with measured longitudes ranging from -41 to -66.

SHOCK MEASUREMENT based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery tracking the wider, faint front which precedes the bulk of this CME. This measurement does not capture the entire shock feature observed in both coronagraphs, and instead follows the leading edge of the shock best, missing the widest portions of the partial halo.

SHOCK measurement based on the approximate source location tracking the faint, wider feature surrounding the bulk portion of this CME. This measurement is preliminary due to limited coronagraph imagery and the measured parameters may vary.
Measurement of the bulk of the CME based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT

SHOCK measurement following the faint feature surrounding the bright bulk portion. The outermost, widest feature of the shock is not included in this measurement. Measured parameters based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Very uncertain analysis based on the fit with ONE coronagraph only (SOHO) since there is no imagery from STEREO A COR2 because of an extensive data gap and the source is backsided, based on the coronal signatures. The range of possible longitudes that produce a decent fit in SOHO is from 115 to 140 degrees.
Preliminary analysis based on the SHOCK of the CME. Higher degree of uncertainty with parameters due to single-spacecraft analysis.

As the source is visible slightly beyond the western limb, a precise source location is unknown. However, the source is visible near the western limb so a measured longitude of 90 degrees was used. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result of the unknown/far-sided source location. This measurement tracks the brighter leading edge portion and excludes the faint feature preceding this.

Preliminary leading edge measurement using one spacecraft (SOHO) which considers a large latitude to fit visual observations; uncertainty in longitude is quite large and may be as large as +/- 30 degrees.
Analysis based on the best fit in two coronagraphs and confirmed by the location of the associated flare.
Shock front measurement using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 incorporating the southeastward leading edge and western/eastern leading edges simultaneously in one circular-shaped measurement.
Analysis based on the best fit in two coronagraphs and confirmed by one possible source (in STEREO EUV imagery).
SHOCK measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C3

Measurement based on the best fit with SOHO LASCO C3 imagery in SWPC_CAT. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available for a measurement. This measurement primarily tracks the fainter shock feature to the south of the halo, but the leading edge of the bulk is traveling with the shock and the leading edge is indistinguishable from the shock.
Leading edge measurement of the CME out to 18 solar radii using SOHO LASCO C3 and knowledge of the source location using EUV imagery.
Parameters based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 using the source for longitude. There is no STEREO A COR2 imagery available for this event due to a data gap.
Measurement of the faint, outermost SHOCK feature based on the source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
BULK measurement with no STEREO A COR2 imagery available for triangulation, assuming that the eruption is indeed on the Earth facing disk and associated with Active Region 3939 near W58.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.
Uncertain one-coronagraph analysis based on the above source. The width of the jet is less than 10 deg.
Measurement using fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 difference imagery and source location (S17W99) based on UV imagery.

Triangulated measurment between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A, with good confidence in a matched far-sided fit around W120-W130 despite the lack of source observation in SDO AIA, GOES SUVI, or STEREO A EUVI. The brighter bulk of the front in SOHO imagery is notably dimpled inwards, but the outer edges were sharp enough to track the leading edge.
BULK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. This shock feature was not visible in STEREO A COR2

SHOCK measurement of the faint, shock-like feature extending much wider than the brighter bulk, best observed in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery. Only two usable frames of STEREO COR2A are available to triangulate this feature, and its longitude could range E40-E60 around the eruption source at E51.
BULK measurement of the brighter, inner feature of this CME. Triangulates well between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO COR2A imagery near the observed source centered around S20E51.

Updated measurement based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not available and the measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

Measurement of the bulk portion based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This event has an irregularly-shaped leading edge, and the outermost feature was tracked in this measurement.
SHOCK measurement following the outermost, fainter shock feature based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3
One coronagraph analysis (SOHO only) in the absence of STEREO A imagery.

SHOCK measurement using only SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery, as STEREO COR2A beacon running difference imagery does not resolve this front after it resumes from a data gap at 2025-02-06T05:09Z, making triangulation within swpc_cat not possible with real-time imagery. Via visual fitting of this wide shock front, a range of E140-E155 is likely, as further longitudes in either direction make for a poor visual fit of the shock.

BULK measurement using only SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery, as STEREO COR2A beacon running difference imagery does not resolve this front after it resumes from a data gap at 2025-02-06T05:09Z, making triangulation within swpc_cat not possible with real-time imagery. This measurement includes all lobes of the more dense bulk following the shock.

Measurement of the leading edge using only SOHO C2/C3; inclusion of STEREO A COR2A data suggests the eruption originates from W55-65 but is not supported by EUV imagery. Uncertainty in longitude about 25 degrees.

Shock front measurement using only SOHO imagery, encompassing the entire width of the CME in support of solar energetic particle modeling efforts. WSA-Enlil+CONE simulations associated with this measurement are created in support of solar energetic particle modeling purposes and model outputs should not be used for CME trajectory analysis.

Bulk for trajectory analysis using only SOHO imagery focusing on mid-point of the leading edge in the northwest, the northern portion is faster than this measurement and eastern portion (portion representing the ecliptic plane) is slower than this measurement, due to the tilt of CME out of the ecliptic with respect to occulting disk.

BULK. Triangulated measurement of the brightest bulk portion of the leading edge, notably clipping some of the more faint nose off the northern portion in SOHO C3 imagery due to the uneven front. This analysis may be preliminary as further analysis continues.

This is a SHOCK measurement. Parameters based on best fit adjusted from source location using single-spacecraft measurement method. There is no STEREO A COR2 imagery available for this event due to a data gap.

This is an updated BULK measurement with later frames. Parameters are based on the best fit of CME features based on potential source location using single-spacecraft measurement method. There is no STEREO A COR2 imagery available for this event due to a data gap.
Measurement based on approximate source location. CME is too faint to be reliably tracked and triangulated in STEREO A COR2.

Measurement using a very limited number of frames. Parameters based on candidate source location seen in STEREO A EUV imagery and best fit between two frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery. There is a data gap that begins in STEREO A COR2 at 2025-02-27T07:53Z and the leading edge is too diffuse to track after the gap ends at 2025-02-27T09:23Z. The leading edge becomes visible halfway through C2 field of view after the end of a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2, and once it enters the C3 field of view, it is almost entirely blocked by the pylon and cannot reliably be tracked.
Parameters based on the best fit of the BULK of the CME. The leading edge has a slight dimpled shape in STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Very approximate analysis of a faint wider shock mostly seen in coronagraph running difference imagery, which seems to be more farsided. This is also confirmed by the fact that the EUV wave is not seen on the Earth facing side in EUV imagery, but there are signatures of a far-sided EUV wave behind the limb, seen in AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.
Analysis based on the best fit with two coronagraphs confirmed by the location of the most likely source - the associated flare.
Analysis based on the best fit with two coronagraphs. It's somewhat confirmed by the location of the flare (but there seems to be some deflection westward).
Parameters based on best fit of the CME using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Strong deflection is likely due to nearby coronal holes.

Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this event, a triangulated measurement was not available and the measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.

Best fit measurement using several frames of STEREO A COR2, four frames of SOHO LASCO C3, and two frames of SOHO LASCO C2. The leading edge is very faint in SOHO LASCO imagery; it is much more well-defined in STEREO A COR2. This CME visually overlaps with CME:2025-03-07T21:49Z in both SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2.

Measurement using source location seen in UV imagery and best fit between a few frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery. The leading edge is very faint in both coronagraphs and becomes too diffuse to reliably track about halfway through the SOHO LASCO C3 field of view.

Very approximate analysis as this jet was measured with the 10 deg halfwidth using the one-coronagraph method in swpc_cat, based only on SOHO imagery and on the location of the associated flare. While the jet is extremely narrow (<2 degrees half-width, lowest half-width setting in swpc_cat that we have to use is 10 degrees).

Measurement made using the best fit between abundant frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery, as well as consideration of the source location seen in available STEREO A EUV, SDO AIA, and GOES SUVI imagery.

Measurement made using the best fit between abundant frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery, as well as consideration of the source location seen in available STEREO A EUV, SDO AIA, and GOES SUVI imagery.

Uncertain analysis based solely on the best possible fit with two coronagraphs. The high posts-eruptive arcades behind the west limb in STEREO A EUV imagery showing much later than the original coronal signatures of opening field lines indicate the source with the longitude >120 deg. However, no fit was found with longitudes >115 deg and the best fit was obtained with the longitude of 109 degrees. Likely deflection of about 10 to 20 degrees eastward relative to the source at W125 would be caused by a large coronal hole located to the northwest of Active Region 4012 at approximately W125.

Updated measurement using the approximated source longitude of former Active Region 14018, which was estimated to be centered near west 100 degrees at the time of this event. The measured parameters may vary slightly due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Leading edge measurement using one spacecraft assuming the source is associated with an eruption just north of AR 4022.
Parameters based on the SHOCK of the CME using SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery. High uncertainty due to lack of stereoscopic viewpoints.

Parameters based on the BULK of the CME using SOHO LASCO C2 imagery. The front of the bulk is not clearly visible in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery due to the control arm. High uncertainty of parameters due to limited stereoscopic viewpoints.

SHOCK measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery and the one available frame of this event seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery, due to an ongoing campaign. This event is likely far-sided and the source location is unknown. The measured parameters may vary as a result.

BULK measurement using the same longitude as what was measured in the shock measurement. The measured parameters may vary greatly as the bulk portion of this event is difficult to distinguish in STEREO A COR2 imagery. Additionally, this event is likely far-sided so there is no source location to confirm the measured parameters.
Measurement based on the source location.

Measurement made using the source location seen in UV imagery of the Earth-facing disk, three frames of STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery with timestamps 2025-03-25T15:23Z, 2025-03-25T15:38Z, and 2025-03-25T15:53Z, as well as one frame of SOHO LASCO C3 running difference imagery at timestamp 2025-03-25T17:54Z. The leading edge is extremely diffuse in SOHO LASCO C3, which introduces some uncertainty. The leading edge of the CME is more clearly defined in the three frames of STEREO A COR2 than in SOHO LASCO C3. | Analysis of this CME was affected by a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2 and C3 imagery lasting from 2025-03-25T13:42Z to 2025-03-25T17:30Z, reduced image quality of SOHO LASCO C3 frames for timestamps following 2025-03-25T17:30Z, and by the regular overnight data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery which began at 2025-03-25T15:53Z.

SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. This measurement contains a high degree of uncertainty due to the lack of available frames as a result of data gaps in both SOHO and STEREO A COR2.

Measurement of the bulk using several more frames of SOHO LASCO C3 imagery than previously available. There is still only one STEREO A COR2 frame available for this CME, but the fit found using C3 frames the source location aligns well with this one STEREO A COR2 frame.
Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs and confirmed by the location of the associated filament eruption (close to the NW limb).

Best fit measurement of leading edge using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2. Strong northern deflection was visible from the source location seen in UV imagery from SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI, and GOES SUVI, which is reflected in the best fit parameters.
Two spacecraft bulk measurement with high confidence in parameters, good fit relative to observed source location.
Shock measurement in SOHO and STEREO A by encompassing the faint northeast edge in both spacecraft as well as the bright bulk.
Leading edge measurement using two spacecraft to triangulate the longitude out to 14 solar radii.

Measurement based on source location and best fit in several frames of SOHO LASCO C2 and C3. No STEREO A COR2 imagery was available in real time for this CME due to a data gap which began at 2025-04-11T11:23Z.
Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs and confirmed by the coronal signatures (opening of field lines behind the southwest limb).

Approximate analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs, setting the half-width to the swpc_cat tool's minimum 10 degrees. The CME is very narrow (narrower than 10 degrees half-width) so the speed could have been underestimated in this analysis.
Updated measurement using additional SOHO LASCO C3 imagery. Measurement based on the source location.
Measurement based on best fit and source location.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.
Measurement of faint leading edge using source location seen in UV imagery and best fit between a few frames of SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2.
Preliminary leading edge measurement with one spacecraft (STEREO A) assuming the known source is just beyond the western limb; to be confirmed with triangulation when SOHO imagery is available.
BULK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3
Measurement based on source location as well as the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 running difference imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Leading edge measurement using SOHO/STEREO A out to 12 solar radii reworked to ascertain a maximum latitude.
Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Triangulated measurement betweeen SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Only two frames of STEREO A COR2 are usable, so running difference image quality is low, but it is enough to track the front and triangulate.

Single spacecraft 3D measurement with SOHO LASCO C2 only. STEREO A COR2 not available due to a data gap, and the LASCO C3 pylon greatly obscures the CME front in white light and running difference imagery. As such, the latitude and longitude may vary +- 10 degrees in either direction, with good confidence in the southern deflection from the observed source via SDO AIA and GOES SUVI imagery.
Measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Parameters based on best fit in relation to source location. Parameters may vary by +/- 10 degrees due to overlapping features in coronagraph imagery.

Analysis based on the best fit of this narrow jet with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2) and confirmed by the location of the likely source (filament eruption). It looks like the CME is deflecting southward.
Preliminary analysis of the SHOCK using about four frames of GOES CCOR-1 and four frames of SOHO LASCO C3.
Analysis of the BULK using about four frames of GOES CCOR-1, four frames of SOHO LASCO C3, and two frames of STEREO A COR2.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.
Measurement made using best triangulated fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.
Analysis based on the likely source of this CME (filament eruption in/near AR 14115) and confirmed by the good fit with two coronagraphs (STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C3).

Approximate analysis encompassing this whole event (which possibly consists of two consecutive CMEs) - encompassing its eastern earlier front and the later, more western (possibly slower) front. Analysis is heavily based on the longitude of the likely source (flare and eruption near Active Region 14114) and on the fits with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2). The fit indicates there was a very significant deflection of the CME northward.
Best fit measurement using multiple frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery, as well as the location of the on-disk source and likely deflection observed in available UV imagery.
Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, front is notably faint and difficult to track.
Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.
Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
Measurement based on triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
One spacecraft measurement assuming some modest westward deflection of about 5 degrees and starting nearby to the source of the eruption in EUV imagery.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

Approximate analysis based on the fit of the two-pronged front with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1). This analysis is confirmed by the location of the likely CME source, which appears to be or or just behind the east limb.
Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is a higher level of uncertainty due to faintness of event.

Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Due to the faint, diffuse nature of this leading edge, some variance in all parameters may exist as tracking the true leading edge is difficult. High confidence in the <10 degree HW.
Best fit measurement using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1, as well as location of the source eruption seen in available UV imagery of the disk.
Best fit measurement of the BULK using several frames of SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1, as well as location of the source eruption seen in available UV imagery of the disk.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
This is an initial measurement with only GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3
Preliminary measurement based on best-fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1

Shock measurement encompassing the outermost leading edge of the halo; width greater than 60 degrees required to fit the entire shape in all coronagraphs, but as the width was increased beyond conventional halo widths (45-to 55), the lemniscate began to fit the CME more skillfully.
Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2.

Best fit measurement using several frames of GOES CCOR-1 and a few frames of STEREO A COR2. The leading edge is extremely diffuse, adding some uncertainty to this measurement. This CME was captured by only one frame of SOHO LASCO C2 in real time, due to a regularly scheduled downlink data gap which began 2025-08-28T20:24Z.
Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. No clear source is observed on-disk here, but good confidence in the coronagraph triangulation on front-sided parameters near E78.
SHOCK analysis. Well-triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, with a notably wider half width of 53 degrees.

BULK measurement update. Triangulated measurement between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. Halo signature in LASCO C2/C3 is notably dimpled and non-circular, especially compared to STEREO A COR2. This analysis is the best fit of the bulk material excluding a southward nose that travels slightly faster than the main front.
UPDATE: Reevaluated to be the SHOCK portion of this CME. Measurement based of fainter, wider, outermost leading edge of the CME.
BULK measurement of the brighter, inner portion of the CME. SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only due to STEREO A COR2 data gap.
Approximate analysis based on the source location as seen in STEREO A EUVI 304/195 and on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2).

Best fit measurement using candidate source location, two frames of SOHO LASCO C2, and one frame STEREO A COR2. There is some uncertainty with this measurement due to the faintness of the leading edge and a data gap in SOHO LASCO lasting from 2025-09-24T09:24Z to 2025-09-24T12:00Z.

Analysis including both the southern and the northern lobe of this CME and based on a fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2). GOES CCOR-1 coronagraph (specifically the northern lobe of this CME as seen from CCOR-1) does not fit with this analysis.

Analysis based on the fit of this narrow jet with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 and in alignment with the possible source - a C class flare from AR14232. No good fit with this analysis for CCOR-1.
Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Later analysis based on a good fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2), also fitting GOES CCOR-1. This analysis is confirmed by the location of the CME source (M class flare from AR 14232), however there seems to be some eastward deflection from the location of this Active Region, based on the fit with coronagraphs.

Approximate/speculative analysis based on the fit with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs and fitting a bit to the east of AR 14232 which is a possible source, so perhapse there is a deflection to the east because of a coronal hole to the west of the Active Region.
Single spacecraft measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3.
Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. An Earth eclipse prevents the use of GOES CCOR-1 during this analysis.
Analysis based on the fit with two coronagraphs, SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.  This analysis is confirmed by the location of the likely CME source - M1.0 flare from AR 14232.

This analysis includes a brighter, more southern lobe and a more faint northern lobe, both of which are better seen in SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs. If the source of this CME is indeed a flare and filament eruption from AR 14232, this analysis suggests a significant SE deflection from the source.
Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.
Leading edge measurement between STEREO and SOHO which showed some level of moderate deflection to the east relative to the source location of the eruption.

Measurement of SHOCK using source location seen in available UV imagery and best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not captured in real time by STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2025-10-21T19:38Z.

Measurement of BULK using source location seen in available UV imagery and best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not captured in real time by STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2025-10-21T19:38Z.

Measurement of the SHOCK using the location of the candidate source seen in available UV imagery and best fit between a handful of frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not captured in real time by STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2025-10-22T19:23Z.

Measurement of the BULK using the location of the candidate source seen in available UV imagery and best fit between a handful of frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. Not captured in real time by STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2025-10-22T19:23Z.
Measurement of the brighter bulk feature based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

SHOCK measurement based on the source longitude. Due to a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this event, the shock front associated with this event is not seen in STEREO A. The measured parameters may vary as a result.

Updated SHOCK analysis triangulation between STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1. Due to the oblong shape of the shock feature, the front does not fit well in all 3 coronagraphs together. STEREO A COR2 has the better viewing angle of the front with its spacecraft position around W49, so this fit focuses on capturing the full front in COR2A and fits most of the front, focusing on the eastern side, in LASCO C2/C3 and CCOR-1.

A rather speculative one-coronagraph (LASCO) analysis because the CME is not seen in STEREO coronagraph due to a large data gap. The latitude (and hence the speed) could be different. The latitude of 24 deg is chosen to correspond to the latitude of former AR 14246 when it was seen on the front side. The Active Region produced multiple more northern CMEs, so this analysis is very approximate.
Very approximate, uncertain one-coronagraph measurement of a fainter wider shock.

Measurement using the best fit between an abundance of frames of SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. Source is not visible in available UV imagery due to current lack of viewpoint coverage for beyond the northeast limb of the Earth-facing disk.
SHOCK measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Leading edge/bulk measurement using GOES SUVI, STEREO A COR2, and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 out to about 23 solar radii.
Shock measurement primarily relying on STEREO Ahead as the CME was not able to be fit in two coronagraphs simultaneously.
Measurement using best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.

Measurement using candidate source location seen in available UV imagery and best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1. Leading edge becomes too diffuse to track about one forth of the way through the SOHO LASCO C3 FOV.

These parameters are based on the best fit of the BULK of the CME using GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. Some deflection may have occurred with the nearby negative polarity coronal hole feature visible on the Earth-facing solar disk.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
These parameters are based on the best fit using SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Final analysis with more imagery. It is based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1) and on the source location of the M3.5 flare. This complex event associated with two flares is treated as a single CME.

SHOCK analysis, best fit triangulation between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 of the faint, wider halo shock in all 3 coronagraphs. Due to the large width of the observed shock front and viewing angle differences between the coronagraphs, this best fit is made using the width in GOES CCOR-1/SOHO LASCO C3 and tracking the edge of the front with less emphasis on the width in COR2A. Measurable SOHO LASCO C2 imagery not yet available due to a downlink gap.

Triangulated measurement between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2; SOHO LASCO C2/C3 not yet available due to ongoing downlink gap. The CME front is somewhat irregularly shaped, as such this triangulation captures the majority of the bulk material as best as possible.
Best-fit measurement based on limited imagery from STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
Best-fit measurement of the SHOCK feature based on running difference imagery from STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
Measurement of the inner, brighter bulk portion based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
SHOCK measurement of the faint, wider feature surrounding the bulk of this event. Measured parameters based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Measurement of the shock front out to 13 solar radii.
Updated bulk measurement out to 25 solar radii.
BULK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
Measurement of the SHOCK feature using the best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
Measurement of the BULK using source location seen in available UV imagery and best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2, and GOES CCOR-1.
Measurement using best fit between several frames of SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 and the candidate source location seen in available UV imagery.

A tentative analysis with one coronagraph (SOHO LASCO), based on a very approximate source location (N45W20). In the absence of STEREO A imagery due to long data gap this is the best that can be done.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

Parameters based on best fit of the BULK of the CME, however the fit is better in STEREO A COR2 imagery than in SOHO or GOES imagery due to triangulation limitations. The half-width appears too wide for the visible bulk feature in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery compared to the visible bulk feature in STEREO A COR2 imagery. This may be due to limited viewpoints of the full CME.
Parameters based on best fit of the SHOCK.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
Measurement based on best-fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. GOES CCOR-1 was not used as a majority of the propagation of the CME was covered by a data gap.

Approximate analysis based on the fit of the front with SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs, confirmed by the possible location of the likely source (eruption of prominence off/behind the NE limb).

Approximate analysis based on the fit of the front in three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1). The source is likely one of the lobes of what looks like a three-pronged prominence eruption from/behind the NE limb, seen starting at 2025-11-29T05:36Z in GOES SUVI 304.

A very speculative analysis of the faint full halo shock front of this CME, based on the assumption that the longitude of the CME is approximately -130 degrees (since it is seen as full halo in STEREO A). However, there are multiple other fast CMEs happening simultaneously with this (including a faster 2025-11-29T05:48Z CME), so the shock may be associated with one of these other CMEs.
Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

The CME front is lopsided due to the eruption deflection and partial overlap with CME 2025-11-29T16:00Z. Best attempt at triangulating and following the leading edge direction is taken between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2, which does miss some material on the northern edge that cannot fit in the swpc_cat tool's width due to the elongated CME shape, as such the half-width may be wider than 27 degrees.

Updated bulk measurement based on the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. This measurement focuses on the bright portion of the CME and excludes the faint outer shock feature.
SHOCK measurement focusing on the faint feature surrounding the bulk portion. Measured parameters based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Measurement based on the source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Parameters based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Analysis of the very faint likely shock front based on the fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2). The source is far-sided.

Very approximate analysis of the faint wide shock of this CME with one-coronagraph method (SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs), based on the fit of the partial halo front with coronagraphs. The source is far-sided and the exact longitude is not known.

Measurement following the wider feature seen in SOHO LASCO imagery. The measured parameters were obtained between the approximate source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Bulk measurement tracking the inner, brighter feature based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
SHOCK measurement following the fainter, outer feature. The measured parameters were obtained from the best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Analysis of the fainter leading shock front with one coronagraph method (SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1) based on the shape of the front; this analysis fits the location of the source - flare and eruption near AR 14334.
Approximate, one-coronagraph (SOHO LASCO) analysis of the eastern lobe of this complex eruption.

Very speculative analysis since the only possible (and extremely minor) source seems to be on/close/behind the SE limb in SDO AIA 171 but (a very uncertain) fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2 and one or two rather questionable timestamps of STEREO A COR2) produces a fit of ~70 deg of longitude.

Half width less than 10 degrees. Single spacecraft 3D analysis due to lack of COR2A imagery and CCOR-1 pylon obstruction, using the observed flare source S16W04 as a basis. However, observed deflection of the CME in SDO AIA imagery and the inability to triangulate with other coronagraphs makes this analysis speculative, and the latitude/longitude could easily range within +-10 degrees.
Measurement based on potential source location using GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Shock measurement based on the potential source location, with adjustment to best fit the shock of the CME in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C3 imagery.
Parameters based on best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
Approximate analysis of the wide faint shock front based on the fit with two coronagraphs (STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1) in the absence of SOHO LASCO imagery that is expected to be available later.

Approximate analysis based on the fit with all three coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1) and on the location of the flare, made once SOHO LASCO imagery became available. Analysis is complicated by the CME having two overlapping lobes, one more to the SE and another a bit more central.
Approximate analysis based on the fit of the front with two coronagraphs (STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1) and confirmed by the location of the likely source (minor filament eruption).

Analysis based on the fit of the narrow front with two coronagraphs (STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C3). Very well corresponds to the likely source - an eruption from (N15E10), with significant northern deflection, likely due to a large coronal hole being just to the south of the eruption site.
Measurement based on source location and best fit in GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.
Analysis based on the location of the source (C6.0 flare and eruption in the former Active Region 14351, seen in STEREO A EUV imagery after 2026-01-31T04:50Z.
Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. There is some degree of uncertainty in this measurement, and longitudes ranging from W77 to W90 were measured.
Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
SHOCK measurement based on best fit of the SHOCK feature in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.
Measurement based on best fit of the leading edge in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The CME is best visible in STEREO A COR2.
Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.
Measurement of the faster, fainter halo shock feature seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Updated measurement of the leading edge based on the best fit between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Preliminary analysis based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO C2/C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery in SWPC_CAT.
Updated parameters based on SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery with matching to possible features in STEREO A COR2 following the data gap. Possible deflection within the FOV due to nearby CH.

Final analysis of the brighter bulk of this CME based on the location of the X-class flare and associated eruption, made with fully available coronagraph imagery from SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 and a couple of GOES CCOR-1 images.
A very speculative analysis of the faint shock of this CME using mostly the SOHO LASCO imagery since there was no good fit with two coronagraphs (SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2).
Measurement based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2 imagery.
Preliminary shock front measurement using only a few early available frames of GOES CCOR-1.
Measurement based on the on-disk source location.
Measurement of the more symmetric shock front which much better fitting using triangulation relative to the asymmetric bulk.
Analysis based on the fit of the brighter bulk front with three coronagraphs, SOHO LASCO, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.
