Analysis of the faint partial halo shock front with LASCO and GOES CCOR-1, while the shock in STEREO A COR2 does not produce any fit with the other two instruments and seems to be directed westwardly, as seen from STEREO A.
Measurement of the bulk feature based on the source location and best fit between SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Parameters based on best fit of the SHOCK of the CME. This shock fit is slightly narrow of the entire visible shock as seen in STEREO A COR2 due to measurement constraints. These parameters have a higher degree of uncertainty due to proximity to a coronal hole and the nature of eruption.
Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.
Approximate analysis of the faint halo shock front based on the fit with two coronagraphs, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

Updated BULK measurement based on SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Longitude and latitude were based on potential source signature in STEREO A EUVI 304 and 195 along the NW limb following the return of data around 2026-05-26T01:45Z.

Updated SHOCK measurement using potential source location from STEREO A EUVI 304/195. There is a higher level of uncertainty with this analysis due to limited triangulation ability as well as the unique shape of the CME front. This analysis tracks the furthest out portion of the shock (the "nose") of the CME and includes most of the shock that is more in the ecliptic plane, however this measurement also includes unavoidable empty/dead space due to the overall shape of the shock front and the restrictions of the SWPC_CAT measuring tool.
Measurement based on best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and longitude fit of previous CME: 2026-05-25T22:12Z.
Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 as well as on visible source location in STEREO A EUVI.
Updated measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
SHOCK measurement based on best fit of the wider shock feature in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

Approximate analysis of the messy, two-lobed bulk front of this CME, based on the fit with three coronagraphs (STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1). There is clear northward deflection from the source location of the M-class flare (N14W13) but the associated erupting filament seems to originate a bit to the west from the flare location and is then seen deflecting northwardly, so the coronal signatures generally confirm this analysis. The half-width of the CME is based on later imagery in STEREO A COR2, as in coronagraphs there is/are later, wider, lobe(s) of this CME that seem to be integral part of it.
Approximate analysis of the fainter and wider partial halo front best seen in GOES CCOR-1 but also seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph.
A remeasurement of the two-lobed bulk front with more imagery.

Approximate analysis of the faint partial halo shock front of this CME based on the fit with GOES CCOR-1 coronagraph, in which this front is seen clearer. LASCO imagery is also used. The front is not seen/clear in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph.
Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Triangulated shock front between SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and one available frame of STEREO A COR2 where the shock is visible. The shock front is complex and has two distinct edges, this analysis is of the "brighter" SE-directed inner shock (ahead of and distinct from the bright LE), excluding a faint more SW-directed shock edge as fitting both in one does not yield a good fit.
Updated bulk measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Shock measurement following the outermost faint feature observed in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. A default half-width of 45 degrees was used as the shock feature is not observed in STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Bulk triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and two available frames of STEREO A COR2. Front appears slightly more wide in COR2A than C2/C3.

Preliminary shock analysis with only several available GOES CCOR-1 frames. Due to the limited frames and full halo presentation, the shock width could vary, impacting speed. Current preliminary analysis of the shock is consistently around 1200 km/s, with high confidence in the latitude and longitude.
Preliminary shock STEREO A COR2 only analysis.
Updated leading edge measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
Parameters based on best measurement of the BULK of the CME. Likely deflection within the FOV due to proximity to coronal holes.
Parameters based on best fit of the SHOCK as seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery. No clear shock features visible in available GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

Triangulation between GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2. The CME structure is complex, and in COR2 two fronts to the NE are observed, with a brighter core following the more faint, outer leading edge that matches with the brightest outer feature in CCOR-1. As such, this fit encompasses that outermost leading edge in COR2A with CCOR-1's leading edge.

GOES CCOR-1 only shock analysis, somewhat speculative due to the asymmetric shape and poor visibility. The shock may be visible in STEREO A COR2, but is either too faint or obscured by the bright bulk, and does not track well with the more clear shock front observed in GOES CCOR-1. As such, single spacecraft is used with the same longitude as the LE to approximate, and parameters could vary as a result.
BULK parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There may be some uncertainty with these parameters due to limited stereoscopic viewpoints.
SHOCK parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There may be some uncertainty with these parameters due to limited stereoscopic viewpoints.
This fit is more speculative than normal due to the faintness of the leading edge in STEREO A COR2. This CME is mostly missed by STEREO A COR2.
Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Parameters based on best fit using SOHO LASCO C2, C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The CME deflects further south as it progresses outwards in the field of view.
SHOCK SOHO LASCO C2 only 3D analysis, using the source longitude at W68 as an estimate. With no COR2A available for triangulation at the time of analysis, parameters could vary slightly.
Measurement based on the best fit between STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

Measured longitude based on the source location. Due to a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, a triangulated measurement was not available. The measured parameters may vary slightly as a result.
BULK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

SHOCK analysis, somewhat speculative using SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only (CCOR-1 observes the shock, but does not track perfectly between what is seen in LASCO, with no usable STEREO A COR2 imagery available to triangulate). This analyzed longitude is significantly far from the eruptive source around W54 degrees, but the entire shock front does not otherwise fit within the swpc_cat tool at more western longitudes.
Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.
